body:
Decided and implemented as **ADR-0114**. The consumer survey this issue asked for first is what made the casing call easy, and it also corrected two of the issue's own premises.

## The survey

**Nothing branches on a field code.** objectui has exactly one consumer — `extractFieldErrors` in `react/src/utils/error-message.ts` — and it reads `field` and `message`, touching `code` only as the last fallback in `firstString(rec.message, rec.error, rec.code)`; its own comment says an untranslated enum in the UI reads as a bug. The framework has no product-code branch at all; every match is a test asserting an emitter. So "form UIs may already string-match" is not a constraint, and the casing could be chosen on principle.

**The vocabulary is more coherent than "four dialects."** Six emitters, 24 distinct codes, and the overlaps are semantically consistent — `required` means the same thing in all five places that emit it, as do `max_length`, `min_value`, `invalid_option`. What was missing was a *schema*, not a decision about which dialect wins.

## Decisions

**Lowercase `snake_case`, deliberately not ADR-0112's SCREAMING.** A top-level code names the condition the *request* hit; a field-level code names the *constraint* the value violated — and constraints are declared in the metadata's own snake_case, so `max_length` the code and `max_length: 50` the property are the same word on purpose. Going SCREAMING would sever that to buy consistency with a vocabulary D6 deliberately separated.

**`FieldErrorCode`, closed, 27 members**, and `FieldErrorSchema.code` validates against it. No ledger tier unlike ADR-0112: a constraint *kind* is a property of the type system, so a service adds a member rather than inventing one. `FieldValidationError.code` (objectql — a hand-listed literal union, the shape that bit batch 2 from two packages away) and `FieldCoerceError.code` (rest — a bare `string`) now reference the catalog, so the three cannot drift.

**Zod is mapped at the boundary.** Your item 2, with a wrinkle the issue did not know about: `too_small` *is* resolvable — Zod v4 issues carry `origin`, so it splits cleanly into `min_length` / `min_value` / `min_items`, and `format` splits `invalid_format` into `invalid_email` / `invalid_url` / `invalid_format`.

The one case `origin` cannot settle turned out to be a real bug rather than a naming choice: **Zod reports a missing required property as `invalid_type`** (expected string, received undefined), so the passthrough made a form mark a *missing* input as the wrong *type*. Missing and wrong-typed are byte-identical on the issue — v4 carries `expected` and a message but **not the offending value** — so the mapper takes the parsed input as an optional argument and walks the issue path. A caller that cannot supply it keeps `invalid_type` rather than a guess read out of Zod's message text, which would make the wire contract depend on Zod's phrasing.

That detail only surfaced because the tests drive **real** `safeParse` calls: the first draft read `issue.input`, and a real parse showed that branch could never fire.

**`unknown_param` → `unknown_field`**; `ActionParamIssue.code` references the catalog instead of its own literal union.

## Your item 3, split

The **element schema** lands — that is the half that makes a validation body assertable, and it is done.

The **`fields` vs `fieldErrors` rename does not**, and this is the one place I stopped short deliberately. `fields` is right (six emitters, the client and the console all say it; nothing has ever emitted `fieldErrors`), but it is an **authorable key**, and the contract guard in `build-schemas.ts` (#3733, ADR-0104) blocked the bare rename — correctly: these schemas are not `.strict()`, so Zod silently strips an unknown key, and anyone still writing the old name would get a clean parse and a value that never takes effect. Doing it properly needs a `retiredKey()` tombstone, a D2 conversion so `os migrate meta` can rewrite consumers, and a major changeset with the FROM → TO mapping. That is a change of its own, not a rider. The property now carries a banner naming the mismatch and the machinery its retirement needs — declaring the wrong name loudly beats renaming it quietly.

## Also recorded rather than fixed

The top-level catalog still carries six field-shaped members (`INVALID_FIELD`, `MISSING_REQUIRED_FIELD`, `INVALID_FORMAT`, `VALUE_TOO_LONG`, `VALUE_TOO_SHORT`, `VALUE_OUT_OF_RANGE`) — your fourth "vocabulary." They stay: removing a member breaks a vocabulary two batches just stabilised, and `VALIDATION_ERROR` + a `fields[]` entry is already the honest top-level answer. The consequence is that `invalid_format` exists at both levels, which the catalog test admits as the single **declared** overlap rather than papering over — an unlisted overlap fails, because that is how a field member gets added by copying a top-level one.

## Guard note, discharged

`FieldErrorSchema.code`'s banner is gone, replaced by a pointer to the catalog.

Two of the repo's own gates caught real drift, both kept as evidence in comments: a live route's test had pinned the `invalid_type` passthrough, and two doc examples put top-level concepts in a field-code position — one of which the catalog answers exactly (`invalid_transition`).

PR incoming; spec 6899, objectql 1171, rest 502 green, plus the full `turbo run test` and the dogfood shards.
